learn.hook: How can a huge country like India fit on one page of your atlas? With a map!
points: A globe is a small round model of the Earth. It shows the true shape of the Earth and its continents and oceans.
A map is a flat drawing of the whole Earth or a part of it, like a city, a state or a country.
Maps are easy to carry and can show a small place in great detail, which a globe cannot.
Three key parts of a map are distance (scale), direction and symbols. A key or legend explains the symbols.
Physical maps show natural features like mountains and rivers; political maps show countries, states and cities; thematic maps show one theme, like rainfall or crops.

example.q: On a map, 1 cm stands for 10 km. Two towns are 4 cm apart on the map. How far apart are they really?
steps: The scale tells us 1 cm on the map = 10 km on the ground.
The towns are 4 cm apart, so multiply: 4 × 10 km.

learn.reallife: Metro route maps, map apps on phones and the map of your school drawn for Sports Day are all maps with symbols and directions.

quiz.q: What is a globe?
options: A flat drawing of a city
A small round model of the Earth
quiz.explain: A globe is a 3-D model of the Earth, so it shows the Earth's real round shape.
quiz.mistake: Confuses a globe with a map or an atlas

quiz.q: Which is the best tool to show the roads around your school in detail?
options: A large-scale map of the area
quiz.explain: A globe is too small to show local roads, but a map of a small area can show every lane.
quiz.mistake: Thinks a globe can show small local details

quiz.q: What does the scale of a map tell us?
options: How map distance compares with real distance on the ground
The name of the map maker
quiz.explain: The scale, like 1 cm = 10 km, links distances on the map to real distances.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up the scale with the legend or the north arrow

quiz.q: On a map, 1 cm = 5 km. Two villages are 6 cm apart on the map. What is the real distance?
quiz.explain: Each centimetre stands for 5 km, so 6 cm stands for 6 × 5 = 30 km.
quiz.mistake: Adds the numbers instead of multiplying

quiz.q: Where on a map would you look to find out what a small tent symbol means?
quiz.explain: The key (legend) lists each symbol and explains what it stands for.
quiz.mistake: Does not know the purpose of the legend

quiz.q: Which type of map would show the states of India and their capitals?
quiz.explain: Political maps show boundaries of countries and states, and cities.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up physical and political maps

quiz.q: On most physical maps, what colour is used for water bodies like seas and lakes?
quiz.explain: Blue is the usual colour for water. Brown is used for mountains and green for lowland plains.
quiz.mistake: Does not know the standard colours used on maps

quiz.q: Why do we use symbols on maps?
options: They show many features in a small space and are easy to understand
They are needed only on globes
quiz.explain: Drawing every building or temple would take too much space, so small symbols stand for them.
quiz.mistake: Thinks symbols are only for decoration

teach.ask: Gappu is holding a globe and a map. 'They both show places! Why do we need both? And how do I read a map?'
teach.praise: Wow! Now I know a globe is a round model and a map is a flat drawing with scale, direction and symbols. I can read my atlas!
teach.nudge: But how do I know what the little pictures on a map mean, or how far apart two places really are?

learn.hook: If you stand facing the rising Sun, which direction is behind you? Let's find out!
points: The four main or cardinal directions are North (N), South (S), East (E) and West (W).
Between them are four intermediate directions: North-East (NE), South-East (SE), South-West (SW) and North-West (NW).
The Sun rises in the east and sets in the west, which helps us find directions outdoors.
A compass has a magnetic needle that always points to the north.
Most maps show north at the top, marked with an arrow and the letter N.

example.q: Asha stands facing the rising Sun in the morning. Which direction is on her left?
steps: The Sun rises in the east, so Asha is facing east.
When you face east, north is on your left and south is on your right.

learn.reallife: Pilots, ship captains and trekkers in the Himalayas use compasses and maps so they never lose their way.

items.text: The direction between north and east is ___.

games.title: Direction check
items: The four cardinal directions are north, south, east and west.
These four are the main directions.
South-West lies between south and west.
Intermediate directions sit between two cardinal ones.
On most maps, north is shown at the bottom.

If you face north, east is on your right.
Facing north, east is to the right and west to the left.
The opposite of east is north.
The opposite of east is west.

quiz.q: How many cardinal (main) directions are there?
quiz.explain: North, south, east and west are the four cardinal directions.
quiz.mistake: Counts the intermediate directions as cardinal ones too

quiz.q: In which direction does the Sun rise?
quiz.explain: Every day the Sun rises in the east and sets in the west.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up sunrise and sunset directions

quiz.q: Which direction lies between south and east?
quiz.explain: The intermediate direction between south and east is called south-east (SE).
quiz.mistake: Picks a direction made of the wrong pair

quiz.q: What does the needle of a magnetic compass point to?
quiz.explain: A compass needle is magnetic and always settles pointing north-south, with its marked end to the north.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the compass needle follows the direction you face

quiz.q: Ravi faces south. What is behind him?
quiz.explain: North is opposite to south, so it is behind him.
quiz.mistake: Does not recall which directions are opposite

quiz.q: Meena faces west at sunset. Which direction is on her right?
quiz.explain: Facing west, north is to the right and south is to the left.
quiz.mistake: Uses the rule for facing north while facing west

quiz.q: What is the direction opposite to north-east?
quiz.explain: Opposite of north is south and opposite of east is west, so opposite of north-east is south-west.
quiz.mistake: Changes only one part of the direction

quiz.q: On a map with north at the top, a lake is at the bottom-left corner. Where is the lake?
quiz.explain: Bottom is south and left is west, so bottom-left is south-west.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up left and right on a map

teach.ask: Gappu is lost in the playground. 'Which way is which? How can I find north?'
teach.praise: Thank you! The Sun rises in the east, and my compass needle points north. I'll never get lost now!
teach.nudge: But what can I look at in the sky, or carry in my pocket, to find the directions?

learn.hook: Imagine drawing lines around a ball like belts. On the Earth, these belts are called latitudes!
points: Latitudes, also called parallels, are imaginary lines running east-west around the Earth, parallel to the Equator.
The Equator is the 0° latitude. It divides the Earth into the Northern and the Southern Hemisphere.
Latitudes are measured in degrees from 0° at the Equator to 90° at each Pole: 90°N is the North Pole and 90°S is the South Pole.
Important parallels: Tropic of Cancer (about 23.5°N), Tropic of Capricorn (about 23.5°S), Arctic Circle (about 66.5°N) and Antarctic Circle (about 66.5°S).
Places near the Equator are hot; places near the Poles are very cold. The Tropic of Cancer passes through the middle of India.

example.q: A place is at 0° latitude. What can you say about it?
steps: The Equator gets the Sun's rays almost straight overhead through the year.
So the place is on the Equator and is usually hot.
example.answer: It lies on the Equator and is generally hot.

learn.reallife: India lies fully in the Northern Hemisphere, and the Tropic of Cancer runs across states like Gujarat, Madhya Pradesh and West Bengal.

quiz.q: What is the latitude of the Equator?
quiz.explain: Latitudes are counted from the Equator, so the Equator is 0°.
quiz.mistake: Thinks latitudes are counted from the Poles

quiz.q: What is the latitude of the North Pole?
quiz.explain: Latitudes go up to 90° at each Pole; the North Pole is 90°N.
quiz.mistake: Thinks latitudes go up to 180°

quiz.q: Into which two halves does the Equator divide the Earth?
quiz.explain: Everything north of the Equator is the Northern Hemisphere and everything south is the Southern Hemisphere.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up the Equator with the Prime Meridian

quiz.q: Which important line of latitude passes through India?
quiz.explain: The Tropic of Cancer (about 23.5°N) runs across the middle of India.
quiz.mistake: Does not know that India is in the Northern Hemisphere, north of the Equator

quiz.q: In which direction do lines of latitude run?
options: From the North Pole to the South Pole
East to west, around the Earth
quiz.explain: Latitudes are circles running east-west, parallel to the Equator.
quiz.mistake: Confuses latitudes with longitudes

quiz.q: Why are latitudes also called parallels?
options: They all meet at the Poles
They are all the same length
They run parallel to the Equator and never meet
They are drawn only on maps of India
quiz.explain: Parallel lines stay the same distance apart and never meet; latitudes are like that.
quiz.mistake: Thinks latitudes meet at the Poles like longitudes

quiz.q: Which place is likely to be the coldest?
quiz.explain: Places close to the Poles get slanting sunlight and are very cold.
quiz.mistake: Thinks a bigger latitude number means a hotter place

quiz.q: The Tropic of Capricorn is at about 23.5° in which hemisphere?
quiz.explain: The Tropic of Capricorn is south of the Equator; the Tropic of Cancer is north.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up the Tropic of Cancer and the Tropic of Capricorn

teach.ask: Gappu looks at the globe. 'What are these flat circles going around it? Which one is the Equator?'
teach.praise: Super! Latitudes are parallel circles, starting at 0° at the Equator and going up to 90° at the Poles. Now I can find the Tropic of Cancer!
teach.nudge: Which line is at 0°, and how far do the numbers go up to at the Poles?

learn.hook: When it is noon in India, it is still early morning in London. How? The answer lies in longitudes!
points: Longitudes, also called meridians, are imaginary half-circles running from the North Pole to the South Pole.
The Prime Meridian is 0° longitude. It passes through Greenwich, near London. Longitudes go from 0° to 180° east and 180° west.
The Prime Meridian and the 180° line divide the Earth into the Eastern and Western Hemispheres.
The Earth spins once in about 24 hours, turning 360°. So it turns 15° in one hour, and 1° in 4 minutes.
Indian Standard Time (IST) is based on the 82°30'E (82.5°E) longitude. IST is 5 hours 30 minutes ahead of Greenwich time. Long ago, Indian astronomers used a prime meridian passing through Ujjain.

example.q: It is 12 noon at Greenwich (0°). What time is it in India by IST?
steps: India's standard meridian is 82.5°E, east of Greenwich.
The Earth turns 15° each hour, so 82.5 ÷ 15 = 5.5 hours, that is 5 hours 30 minutes.
Places to the east are ahead in time, so add 5 h 30 min to 12 noon.

learn.reallife: When your cousin in London video-calls you after school at 5:30 pm IST in winter, it is only 12 noon for her! (In summer, London moves its clocks one hour ahead.)

quiz.q: What is the longitude of the Prime Meridian?
quiz.explain: The Prime Meridian is the starting line for longitudes, so it is 0°.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up the Prime Meridian with India's standard meridian

quiz.q: Through which place does the Prime Meridian pass?
quiz.explain: The Prime Meridian (0°) passes through Greenwich in England.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the modern Prime Meridian passes through India

quiz.q: How many degrees does the Earth turn in one hour?
quiz.explain: The Earth turns 360° in 24 hours, so 360 ÷ 24 = 15° each hour.
quiz.mistake: Divides by the wrong number or confuses hours with degrees

quiz.q: Indian Standard Time is based on which longitude?
quiz.explain: IST is calculated from the 82°30'E (82.5°E) meridian, which passes near Mirzapur in Uttar Pradesh.
quiz.mistake: Confuses a latitude value with a longitude value

quiz.q: How far ahead of Greenwich time is IST?
quiz.explain: India is east of Greenwich, so its clocks are 5 h 30 min ahead.
quiz.mistake: Thinks places to the east are behind in time

quiz.q: Where do all lines of longitude meet?
options: At the North and South Poles
quiz.explain: Meridians are half-circles from Pole to Pole, so they all meet at the Poles.
quiz.mistake: Confuses meridians with parallels, which never meet

quiz.q: It is 6 am at Greenwich (Greenwich Mean Time). What is the time in India by IST?
quiz.mistake: Subtracts the time difference instead of adding

quiz.q: In ancient India, astronomers used a prime meridian that passed through which city?
quiz.explain: Indian astronomers long ago calculated time from a meridian through Ujjain, in today's Madhya Pradesh.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the idea of a prime meridian came only from Greenwich

teach.ask: Gappu is confused. 'Why is my cousin in London eating breakfast when I am eating lunch?'
teach.praise: Now I get it! The Earth spins 15° every hour, so places to the east see the Sun first and are ahead in time. India is 5 h 30 min ahead of Greenwich!
teach.nudge: What line do we start counting longitudes from, and how does the Earth's spinning change the time?
